name: Pale Gunmetal
lede: Pale Gunmetal is ColorHub's English name for Tetsu-iro, a dark grey-green that the traditional Japanese color list names for iron, not for the gun metal alloy.

sections.title: Iron, not gun metal
sections.body:
Wikipedia's list of traditional Japanese colors gives this swatch as Tetsu-iro (鉄色), literally "iron color," describing the dull grey-green sheen of unpolished iron [1]. ColorHub's English rendering, Pale Gunmetal, reaches for a related Western metal word; the Japanese source names the raw ore's surface, not a cast alloy [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 places the swatch in block 151, "dark grayish green," about 4.9 units from that block's centre [2]. The library's nearest other named colors are [[vivid-gunmetal]], 3.0 units away, and [[black-green]], just beyond it [2].

Measured in LCH it reads lightness 22, chroma 6, hue 172 degrees, a dark, barely saturated green [2]. The low chroma keeps the swatch close to neutral on screen, which is why the gunmetal association holds even though the Japanese name is about iron ore rather than a forged alloy [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in 792 of 23,781 paintings, about 3 percent, as photographed [3]. It plays a shadow role in 77 percent of its occurrences, fitting a dark, low-chroma hue [3]. Juan de Flandes and Harald Giersing each carry it at more than nine times the archive's overall rate [3]. It shares canvases more than chance with the color word Gunmetal itself, and its presence peaks around the 1470s [3].
